### Add the private archive of original outputs: spool, journal, verified upload, list and fetch

change `wvpwtwyomouq` · [log `1e85b253070c`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b9b56f5e-fc0e-48ca-a64e-7a46495d814f/1e85b253070c79043fc2d3497ba7105bc2aef2a4ee3e2de781ad9cbcbece4f3d.jsonl.gz)

llm-dlc/tools/artifacts.py is the first piece of the process-plumbing brief (llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing.md, section 2). A producer hands the bytes it made to capture before it shortens, replaces or deletes them. They are sealed once into a spool on disk outside the checkout (~/.local/share/in-the-loop/originals), with a full private inventory of every member's path, type, mode, length and SHA-256, and acknowledged only after the intake record and a SQLite journal have them durably. Small files go into bounded packs, large ones into parts, and an append-only file into segments from which any past prefix restores. A restartable uploader commits each attempt before a byte moves, creates each object only if none is there, reads it back with a credential and compares the original bytes with their name, and writes an immutable receipt last, so a fresh machine can rebuild the catalog from the store alone. Ordinary and restricted originals go to separate private R2 buckets; a restricted occurrence is listed in the ordinary one by a stub with no path. list, show and fetch read with the reader's token into a private cache and work offline on a verified hit; missing, pending, restricted or damaged evidence gives a specific unavailable answer. Nothing in the tool deletes a byte, and ITL_ORIGINALS_OFF=1 switches capture off.

Verified by 33 unit tests (llm-dlc/tools/test_artifacts.py): crashes before and after the intake record, after a put and before the receipt, a lease left by a dead worker, two workers on one object, a store that is offline, that loses its answer, that holds other bytes under the same key or a truncated object, a full disk, reused paths, gaps, unsafe manifests and links, and reads from an empty cache and offline. artifacts.py canary passed 11 of 11 checks on the real buckets on 2026-11-21: custody for both classes, a restore from an empty cache, and each token's limits (the ordinary token refused a restricted key, a PUT and a DELETE; the public Worker and the public traces' token read neither class). The contract is in llm-dlc/specification.md, Original outputs; llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-results.md records where the run stands. Nothing calls capture yet: the runner and collector adapters come next.
